In the Data For Good generative AI white paper, the initial estimated carbon footprint for training the BLOOM model was 30 tonnes CO2eq (based on energy consumption and carbon intensity). When extending the scope to include additional factors such as the consumption of all data center equipment (not just servers), the impact of server manufacturing (considering the lifetime and manufacturing emissions of servers and GPUs), and the development phase (including multiple tests, evaluations, and corrections), the estimated carbon footprint increased significantly.

Specifically, the impact of training alone increased from 30 tonnes CO2eq to 39.3 tonnes CO2eq when accounting for all data center equipment. Adding the manufacturing impact raised it further to 50.5 tonnes CO2eq. Including the development phase added an additional 73.32 tonnes CO2eq, resulting in a total estimated carbon footprint of 123.82 tonnes CO2eq for the full scope.

Thus, BLOOM's estimated training carbon footprint changed from an initial estimate of about 30 tonnes CO2eq to a full-scope estimate of approximately 123.82 tonnes CO2eq, which is about four times higher than the initial naive estimate.
